note: Attacker-controlled bytes are accepted as the TLS transcript for the client handshake path.
A fresh SSL client object is created to consume the supplied transcript.
The attacker bytes are written into the memory BIO that backs SSL_read/SSL_do_handshake.
The crafted transcript drives the handshake state machine into certificate/key processing and session setup.
During cleanup, the reference count on a legacy EVP_PKEY is decremented to zero, triggering object teardown.
The EVP_PKEY teardown reaches the embedded DH object and decrements its reference count again, exposing the double-free/use-after-free condition in the legacy cleanup path.
The vulnerable sink is the DH cleanup path reached from TLS handshake key exchange handling; freeing an already-released DH object causes the ASAN-reported heap-use-after-free WRITE.
